text: Discount costs by intelligence growth: the same work costs fewer dollars as AI gets cheaper per capability
description: Felix 2026-11-23: discount because of intelligence growth. The price of a given level of AI capability falls fast (per-token prices for the same benchmark level have dropped by large factors per year). Two uses: (1) Past: to compare a realized cost from months ago with today's estimates, convert it to what the same work would cost now: cost_now = cost_then · g^(-days/365), where g is the yearly factor by which capability gets cheaper. (2) Future: an idea that is mostly AI work gets cheaper the longer it waits, so priority can account for that: doing it now has a price (paying more today), and waiting has a price (the value arrives later, discounted by the existing annual rate). Where intelligence gets cheaper faster than value is discounted, AI-heavy work that isn't urgent should wait, and human-heavy work doesn't get cheaper. g starts as a configurable assumption, later measured from the harness's own price table over time (same model tier, price per million tokens). Pulls the opposite way of the interest compounding (sibling idea).
